Title: Hi I'm Mike and I'm a CheeseAholic!

Messages.Author: JediMike
Messages.Body:
This is a real tough subject for me because I tend to bounce from side
to side on this often. I rarely play my weenie deck at home because it's
pretty easy to win with it, however put me in a Tournament and YA
BABY!!!! Break out the broom, I'm gonna sweep!!! Well, at least until
recently at Gencon.

Typical Misdirect Presence Weenie bleed was what I played, I've had my
fair share of tourny victories with it, so what else would I play after
flying 1200 miles to play in a "one shot, good night" Championship
tournament RIGHT! I went with Robert Goudie and together we were going
to pound our preys viciously and without regret! We spent the whole
flight "turning cheese" into a Razor Sharp Cheddar! All that mattered
was winning. Nothing wrong with that, right?

It was the most MISERABLE tournament I have ever participated in! And
I've been in over 50.

When they sat Robert Goudie down as my predator in the 1st round my
gut wrenched as the smell of dread and Limburger filled the air. We both
new there was a slim possibility of this, and as we discussed earlier in
the day of how the predator of a weenie VS. weenie battle ALWAYS has the
advantage. After getting my prey down to one pool I was reminded of the
truth in that statement. Weenie Dominate (Robert) swept that table. I
was also reminded why I hate weenie decks.

I did not fair any better in the next two rounds as my Grand predator
in both rounds (two different decks) Chose to Force Awake and Eagle
Sight my death blow attempts to my predator. In short, they didn't want
me on there butt and tried to make it there game goal to prolong it as
long as possible. One of my Grand Preds Forced and Eagled SEVEN times in
a row!!! The weenies were scared as hell that he might make it to the
finals. I now wish he would have! GO JOE!!

Ya know, I just wanted it to be over so I could go back and play "FUN"
games with everyone. After all those turned out to be some of the most
challenging and exciting games of the convention for me. It was good
times with good friends. Not to say I didn't try to win either, I did! I
played challenging decks for fun, to win, and I did win! So why didn't I
take that advice in the Championship? Well lets just say I took alot
from that experience.

Can you easily win with a Weenie deck? No, not always. I believe
SEATING is everything to a weenie deck. If I moved Robert over one
seating position he would have swept the finals, I can't say that about
any other deck in the Finals.

Can you have fun playing a Weenie deck? Honestly, even if I win it's
not fun anymore, and it's definitely not fun getting taken out in 3
turns, I hate it.

Can you earn the respect of you fellow players playing Cheese Decks?
There are those who would say: "I don't care". Me personally, I so enjoy
a creative and multifaceted victory.......the kind that play groups make
legend forever.

Ok, my parting shot on weenie decks and I'll leave you to your own
conclusion: I was teaching a new player the game (my Wife) and I wanted
to start her with something simple and something she could possibly win
with......Ahh yes the Presence Misdirect Bleed. So after she swept the
table in a 1/2 hour she turn to me and said: "Well that wasn't very much
fun, where's the strategy in that?" Kind of ironic coming from a new
player I wanted to have win so I could get her into the game. Well, Im
on the wagon, my deck is dismantled and it's on to other tried and true
decks for tourneys, and hopefully some new and inventive ones too. This
sediment in based on MY own feelings for ME playing these styles of
decks. I don't discount those players that do, I just hope I'm better
prepared in the game to deal with them............Thats all I gotta say
bout that!

Michael Courtois,
LA CA V:tes Player
And Member of CheeseAholic Anonymous

Messages.Author: David Bowsky
Messages.Body:
Bravo Mike!!

I've never acually played in a sanctioned tourney.. although I have
played in one or two that a friend hosted at local coffee shops and card
stores, and I decided that while tourney play can be extremely fun (I
love to compete and I love to win :) ) I took away a bad taste in my
mouth from both tournaments.

Not only from not winning, but from the mere fact the experience was not
unlike playing in a M:TG game (and please refrain from making this
thread a magic / Jyhad bashing one... It won't be interesting.) where
the people who simply had the most duplication of key combination cards
could easily win.

I of course gravitate more towards theme decks.. Things like my Ravnos
"So you see Dr. Jones, there is nothing you posess which I cannot take
away.." deck

Of course the Mass Reality, Horrid Reality, Assult Rifle, DB rounds
combo is a bit cheesy, but helps when playing against combat decks.

My local group even instigated a house rule limit of 6 cards of a given
type.. to foster creativity and strategy in deck design, as opposed to
the following example.

We recently converted a M:TG player and brought him into our group. My
friend and I usually maintain a surplus of extra cards (in his
possesion) which we freely give to new players as a way of jump starting
thier own decks. Well, this guys deck, and a very well designed one from
a tourny prospective included somewhere upwards of 20 Brainwashes.

The concept here being that his prey has no chance of bringing out vamps
at all (since you can multiple Brainwash a minion in the inactive, and
someone correct this rule if it is wrong..)

The other points of his design were Sudden Reversals for those pesky
Effective Management cards.. And some Malks and Tori's (Including Anson
for the extra Master)
One malk in particular was Victoria (relinquish the edge and gain 2
pool) So he could easily bleed his defensless prey at least once a
turn.. obtain the edge, and sacrifice it for the extra pool. Combat was
handled by things like Majesty, and he had just enough intercept to
prevent buring the Brainwash cards.

As the player unlucky enough to be his prey.. I was fortunate enough
that he got a bad shuffle and I was able to exonerate 3 of my vamps
before the brainwashing began. However, once it began my Lasombra,
Ventrue AT theme deck (Political Seizure being key to the design) was
powerless to resist such flagrant cheese.

The only thing to my benifit was my Succubus Club, the bartering
(particularly with votes, as he didn't seem to have enough to stop the
polititcal deck his predator was playing) worked to my advantage and I
was able to survive long enough to make the game interesting.

I find this sort of play in pick up games uterly offensive. The object
is to have fun, and for me that includes creating an original design
each time I play. I have only duplicated the following decks:

Ravnos (mentioned above)

"Madness of the Bard" (I love this deck, mainly because everyone else
hates that card :) )

"Armageddon" (which I played in the aformention unsanctioned
tournaments, and had a theme!)

and the "Contract On America" (named after the republican "Contract with
America" which was occuring at the time I designed this deck several
years ago. Ventrue / Tori political)

(BTW, in Contract on America II, Kemintiri *does* become the Ventrue
Justicar for those of you familiar with the "Kindred's Most Wanted")

Every other game I have played in I have experimented with original deck
designs, not in the effort to find the perfect one, but in the effort to
extract the most enjoyment. After all, this is a game and I would rather
lose creatively than win with cheese. Which, I suppose is why I have
never played in a real tournament.

So Mike, and all other chees-a-holics come forth and return to what
makes Jyhad the game it is.. not 20 Brainwashes in a single deck, but a
creative original idea, which can almost be played as though a story
were unfolding on the table!

--David
bag...@sonic.net

out badly, I would have ended with only 4 VPs and Joe Churchill would

helpless. I generally feel his deck is stronger than mine but it just
depends on the environment.

Joe's deck wasn't a dedicated weenie stopper. It was a deck devoted to
stopping and destroying anything it wanted to. The fragile weenies were
just an easy and visible target.

>
> Ya know, I just wanted it to be over so I could go back and play "FUN"
> games with everyone. After all those turned out to be some of the most
> challenging and exciting games of the convention for me. It was good
> times with good friends. Not to say I didn't try to win either, I did! I
> played challenging decks for fun, to win, and I did win! So why didn't I
> take that advice in the Championship? Well lets just say I took alot

I lost two of the four rounds I played in. I should have lost 3 or 4.
Anyway, David Tatu's deck in round 3 was a pretty good battle. The 2nd
Tradition and Vote deck in round 2 was a great battle (that I lost).
These two rounds were more fun and challenging than any of the draft or
free play games I participated in. We just had different experiences.
So, what? I don't think it proved anything either way.

> Can you easily win with a Weenie deck? No, not always. I believe
> SEATING is everything to a weenie deck. If I moved Robert over one
> seating position he would have swept the finals, I can't say that about
> any other deck in the Finals.

Sure, in hindsight. But, I had the option of sitting anywhere I wanted
and I sat right where I wanted to. If I had moved over I now think I
could have won. Keith Thompson was saying that he was about to sweep
the table too, if only he'd had one more turn.

> Well, Im
> on the wagon, my deck is dismantled and it's on to other tried and true
> decks for tourneys, and hopefully some new and inventive ones too.

By the way, Mike, your 2 different Stealth Bleed decks are also cheesy
by some people's standards. I think you're going to have to stick to
your ineffictive decks to avoid the stigma.

--
Robert Goudie

SR, however including 20 of a single card in a Jyhad deck in my mind
lacks a certain amount of subtlety and ingeuitity which inmnsho doesn't
really fit in with the theme of the game.

Of course I'm the type of player who will trade votes for favors (and
vice verse when I need the votes) which as far as I know is not against
the rules, but not generally done. (Every time I do this in front of
someone who has never played with me before the make a comment similar

the same card as many times as possible, usually speaking I have no more

ability to react to different decks I am playing against.

Then again I'm also the guy who refuses to use bleed modifiers in
pick-up games.

Personality quirks of mine. I have nothing against bleed mods, but why
use extra cards to increase bleed when there are vamps who have that
natch, and that card space can be used doing something interesting like
Political Siezure, Thanks for the Donation, and having Democritus out.
(Of course I never got that to work correctly :) )

just happens that way. Not in tourneys, but hey.. next time there's one
in the San Francisco area, maybe I'll try. :)

Messages.Author: Eric Pettersen
Messages.Body:
I guess what I hate about certain decks (e.g. Weenie Misdirect Presence
Bleed) is that they play no defense whatsoever. Consequently, if you are
their first prey, the two typical outcomes of the game for you are:

1) You are ousted quickly.

2) You survive the onslaught, but are hanging on by a thread and are
quickly ousted by your original grand-predator. Possibly, you survive
for a while in a crippled state.

So, the game is almost never fun for the prey of the defense-free predator
deck.

In article <37C4CA28...@sonic.net>,
David Bowsky <bag...@sonic.net> wrote:
> What's 7/7??

7/7 as it is commonly refered to, is a set of Rules Team Rules
from July 7th of 1998.

These, along with the Rules Team Rulings of June 23rd of 1998,
were the first new Rulings in quite some time and they
caused significant controversy.

If you think cheese has created a debate, you should use
DejaNews to go back to early July and August of 1998 and
look at the hundreds and hundreds of posts on all sides
of those issues.

Anyway, if you just need to become familiar with the
7/7 Rulings, surf over to:

http://members.tripod.com/~Lasombra

and you can check out each of the last 5 sets of
Rules Team Rulings in their original issuing
condition.

Carpe Noctem.
